thread:
Alice Chen: FYI customer on Private deployment is seeing frequent SSE disconnects and a lot of partial outputs. They report 20-30s into a stream it just cuts with no final event. They attached client logs showing reconnect attempts.

Priya Kapoor: Which customer/environment? VPC or on-prem? Any proxies in front of the ingress?

Alice Chen: AcmeFinance (highly regulated). Private control plane + on-prem inference nodes behind corporate proxy + internal NGINX ingress. They say streams are usually short but longer responses (~> 256 tokens) get truncated.

Miguel Torres: Can you paste the client logs and any proxy/ingress logs? Also which protocol are they using — EventSource/SSE or HTTP chunked streaming?

Alice Chen: Client uses EventSource in a browser wrapper and also provided a Node client based on fetch + ReadableStream. Client log snippet:

```
[stream] connected
[stream] recv: data: {"delta":"Hello"}\n
[stream] recv: data: {"delta":" world"}\n
[stream] error: ECONNRESET
[stream] attempting reconnect in 1s
```

And their NGINX ingress log:

```
upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.12, server: redwood-private, request: "GET /v1/streams/ai HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.2.9:8080/", host: "private.redwood.internal"
```

Dan O'Neill: That upstream message looks like either the private runtime closed the socket or the corporate proxy in front did. On-prem setups commonly have corporate proxies that terminate long-lived connections or buffer responses until a threshold.

Miguel Torres: Also check MTU/MSS. We've seen large token windows + TLS + additional headers cause packet fragmentation; some middleboxes with mismatched MTU (jumbo frames vs 1500) will drop or reset flows. Ask them to test with MTU 1500 or set MSS clamping.

Priya Kapoor: Customer says their infra team confirmed corporate proxy (BlueCorpProxy) with default idle timeout 60s and buffering enabled.

Alice Chen: They tried increasing server keepalive but still see partial outputs (some token batches arrive then ECONNRESET). Any immediate workarounds?

Miguel Torres: Workarounds to suggest to customer:
- Force HTTP/1.1 for the stream endpoint (some proxies downgrade or mux HTTP/2 and drop SSE).
- Disable proxy buffering (nginx: proxy_buffering off) and increase proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout.
- Send lightweight keepalive comments from the server every 15s: `: keepalive\n\n` to prevent idle timeouts.
- Ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Type: text/event-stream are preserved through the ingress.
- If MTU suspected: try `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500` or enable MSS clamping on the firewall.

Dan O'Neill: For on-prem ingress specifically: if they're terminating TLS at a corporate proxy then re-encrypting to the runtime, some proxies buffer the full response to scan for malware. That will break streaming. Ask them to whitelist the runtime endpoint or use proxy pass-through.

Alice Chen: I asked for a repro curl command from their infra. They ran: 
```
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -N "https://private.redwood.internal/v1/streams?model=redwood-1" 
```
They get first few events then connection closed.

Miguel Torres: Good repro. Ask them to try `curl --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -N ...` If that fixes it then HTTP/2 proxying is the likely culprit. Also test `curl --no-buffer` and `--keepalive-time 10`.

Priya Kapoor: Customer tried `--http1.1` and saw better stability for a bit but still occasional resets. They then changed NGINX ingress config: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` and it improved but occasional partial outputs remain.

Miguel Torres: OK we need deeper traces. Alice, collect: 1) runtime logs around the stream session (search by request id or client ip), 2) ingress/proxy logs with upstream response codes and timings, 3) tcpdump on the node to check for RSTs and MSS/MTU fragmentation, 4) client side full raw headers.

Alice Chen: I've requested logs. Customer provided runtime logs showing `Write failed: broken pipe` right after sending chunk 4. No explicit out-of-memory.

Dan O'Neill: That narrows to the TCP layer or proxy closing connection. If runtime is sending and then gets broken pipe, something is sending RST or FIN. Check firewall or IPS that might consider long-lived streams suspicious.

Priya Kapoor: Customer flagged this as P1 due to production impact. They asked if Dedicated vs Private behaves differently for streaming.

Miguel Torres: Yes — differences to note:
- Dedicated (our hosted/reserved capacity) sits in our cloud and uses our managed load balancers which we tune for SSE (idle timeouts, buffering disabled, HTTP/1.1 pinned).
- Private/on-prem passes through customer's ingress and corporate networking — so most streaming issues originate from their middleboxes (proxies, intrusion detection, TLS offload).
- VPC setups may have MTU mismatches if using overlay networks (e.g., AWS ENI + ENI trunking) or if customers enable jumbo frames.

Dan O'Neill: Actionable change for Private customers: provide a short runbook they can give to their infra team (disable buffering, extend timeouts, force http/1.1, keepalive comments, MSS clamping). We should also offer an ingress compatibility checklist for our onboarding docs.

Alice Chen: I've created support ticket RW-2026 and attached the logs. Customer wants a short-term mitigation.

Miguel Torres: Short-term mitigation options to propose to customer:
1) Force `--http1.1` or equivalent on client/ingress so upstream runtime sees un-muxed SSE.
2) Configure ingress/proxy to pass stream through (disable buffering and long timeouts).
3) Add server-side keepalive comments so proxies see steady activity.
4) If corporate proxy is unconfigurable, suggest using a tunnel/VPN from client to runtime (bypass proxy) or use Dedicated until on-prem infra can be fixed.

Priya Kapoor: Customer accepted 1+3 and reported improved success rate. They still see rare disconnects at 3-4% of streams.

Dan O'Neill: We should schedule eng-runtime to add a small periodic keepalive event for Private deployments by default (configurable). That will reduce dependency on customer proxies. Miguel, can you take eng-runtime and eng-network on this?

Miguel Torres: I'll own the eng side. Plan: 1) add optional keepalive comment (config flag) + configurable interval, 2) document recommended ingress settings, 3) add diagnostic flags to log when writes get EPIPE and pair with tcpdump evidence.

Alice Chen: I've communicated the plan to the customer and updated the ticket. They asked about billing/auth side: could token expiry cause mid-stream disconnects?

Miguel Torres: Token expiry would cause the server to respond with a final error event then close. It doesn't cause EPIPE. So these symptoms point to network/proxy resets rather than auth. But ask client to confirm token TTL covers stream lifetime and to check server final reason if available.

ingress-bot: Incident note: RW-2026 escalated to eng-runtime and eng-network. Priority: P1 (customer impact).

Priya Kapoor: Customer asked for repro steps we can include in runbook. Suggested snippet for infra teams: 
```
# quick checks for SSE streaming stability
1) Ensure ingress preserves `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`.
2) Disable buffering in NGINX: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;`
3) Increase timeouts: `proxy_read_timeout 360s; proxy_send_timeout 360s;`
4) Force HTTP/1.1 for the stream path: `proxy_http_version 1.1;` and `chunked_transfer_encoding on;`
5) Add MSS clamping on firewall if MTU mismatch suspected: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`
6) If using corporate proxy that does TLS termination, whitelist runtime endpoints or allow pass-through for the path.
7) Use curl for repro: `curl --http1.1 --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -N 'https://private.redwood.internal/v1/streams?model=redwood-1'`
```
Miguel Torres: I'll draft a short KB article for Private/Dedicated differences and include the runbook. We should also add a note in onboarding templates for customers setting up private infra.

Alice Chen: Customer confirmed enabling `proxy_buffering off` + keepalives reduced failures to ~0.5%. They've temporarily moved to Dedicated for critical lanes while we implement runtime keepalive flag for Private.

Dan O'Neill: Good. Follow-ups: Miguel to propose runtime change by next sprint, Priya to update onboarding docs, Alice to close RW-2026 once runtime flag is available and customer validates.

Alice Chen: Marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if customer sees regressions after runtime change. :white_check_mark:
